centralClaimAdjudications.theQuestion: Is declaring-which-it-applies sufficient, or does a contract that contradicts itself at a load-bearing position need escalating as a detected conflict under freeze section 8?
centralClaimAdjudications.ruling: SUFFICIENT TO NOT BLOCK. Incomplete against this corpus's own established precedent. Recorded as IR-RT24-N04 with a named narrowest repair.
reasoningForNotBlocking: Freeze section 8 (cited by section and content anchor per the dispatch instruction, because IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md is under concurrent edit) states the escalation limb as a PROPERTY, not a list: 'They may escalate only a named residual or a detected conflict with a binding artifact.' The section then adds, in text dated 2026-08-03 anchored at 'IR-C2V4-01 is escalable, and this list did not say so.': 'It qualifies under this section's other limb -- a detected conflict with a binding artifact -- and an implementer raising it is correct', and concludes 'an enumeration of named items goes stale silently, while the limb stated as a property -- a detected conflict with a binding artifact -- covered the case correctly without being edited.' A self-contradiction inside a binding artifact is a fortiori a detected conflict with it: no implementation can conform to both statements. It is therefore ALREADY escalable, by the property limb, without being added to any list.

The disagreement is MEASURED rather than noted. planIdNestedClosureRestatementsCompared and planIdNestedClosureRestatementsDisagreeing are recomputed every run and are bound into RT24-A-RES-08's checker-owned boundary clause, so if RESOLVED-INPUTS is repaired, or a second restatement drifts, the numbers move and the artifact fails until it is updated. That is exactly the anti-staleness property section 8 says the property limb has and a named list does not.

The choice made is the PERMISSIVE one. Applying nestedClosure's 5 keys admits more grants than tag 10's 4 would, so the choice cannot hide the open parameters map. The closure conclusion is identical under either reading, and v24 says so.
v24 correctly disclaims authority to amend RESOLVED-INPUTS and does not amend it. Inventing the other side of a contract it does not own is the failure mode this corpus exists to catch.
reasoningForWhyItIsStillIncomplete: This corpus has an established disposition for a defect in a contract one does not own, and v23 used it: the D9 reason-code gap was published with a successor REQUESTED-NOT-ADDED carrying a complete proposal -- deficiency id, reason code, remedy text -- plus a justification measured against D9's own rules. v24 does not do the equivalent for RESOLVED-INPUTS. It records the disagreement and names which statement it obeys, and stops there. No successor request, no proposed resolution, no statement of which of the two statements it believes is the defective one.

The asymmetry is visible in the machine-checked authority record. $.authority carries mayAmendD9Vocabulary: false, mayAmendOperabilityGates: false and mayAmendThreatModel: false. It carries NO entry for RESOLVED-INPUTS -- the one contract in which this artifact actually detected a conflict. The disclaimer exists only in prose (RT24-A-RES-01.whyNotRepairedHere and nestedClosureRestatementAudit.whatItFound). The boolean an instrument could check is the one that is missing.

Freeze section 8's own history is the argument: the named list 'did not say so' for IR-C2V4-01 and had to be amended after a litmus rehearsal reached it. Relying on a reader to derive escalability from the property limb is exactly what failed there.
centralClaimAdjudications.narrowestRepair: Add a RESOLVED-INPUTS successor request in the REQUESTED-NOT-ADDED shape v23 used for D9 -- naming the two conflicting statements verbatim, stating which is believed defective and why, and proposing the resolution -- and add mayAmendResolvedInputs: false to $.authority so the disclaimer is a checked boolean rather than prose. Neither changes any measurement and neither requires touching RESOLVED-INPUTS.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: Non-blocking. The conflict is escalable by construction under section 8's property limb and is measured rather than noted, which is the substance of the obligation. The missing successor request is a departure from the corpus's own precedent and is recorded.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: float 218/0, bool<-0|1 71/0, int<-bool 196/0 -- 485 mutations, 0 admitted, 0 collateral, 0 unruled leaves; 50/50 selftest mutations each asserting finding id AND position; --part a and --part b each exit 0; separability holds.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: ALL VERIFIED, BY THIS REVIEWER'S OWN SWEEP AND OWN SEPARABILITY PROBES.

reviewerLeafCensus.note: The banner reports scalar leaves 2817 and guarded int/bool 414; 218 + 196 = 414. Confirmed.

reviewerThreeArmSweep.method: The reviewer imported the checker as a module, rebuilt its context exactly as main() does, and classified every mutation against the FULL run_all -- not against type_findings alone. Classification: ADMITTED (zero findings), REJECTED-BY-POSITION (a finding naming the mutated JSON path), REJECTED-COLLATERAL (findings, none naming the path -- explicitly NOT counted as a defence).
reviewerThreeArmSweep.assessment: Every one of 485 type mutations is rejected by a finding that names its own JSON path. Zero collateral, so the corpus hazard of a collateral-rejected leaf reaching green after unrelated edits does not arise here. The 'unruled 0' claim is consistent.

selftest.reviewerRun: python3 -I -B check-retention-custody-v24.py --selftest in a clean probe tree: '50/50 mutations caught by their own named check', three sweep lines, SELFTEST-PASS, exit 0.
selftest.assertionStrength: Confirmed strong. Each case requires BOTH the expected finding id AND the mutated JSON path in the finding text; a non-zero exit alone is never accepted. Line 3921 additionally binds the case's asserted id to SELFTEST_ASSERTED_FINDING_ID, and lines 1795/2072 bind each DECLARED expectedFindingId to that same table -- so a declared expectation and an asserted one cannot drift apart. The selftest is dispatched BEFORE findings return, so a dirty base yields SELFTEST-NOT-RUN at exit 3 rather than a green banner over a suite that never ran.

nonBlockingObservations.severity: non-blocking; the strongest finding of this review
nonBlockingObservations.statement: The one checker-side literal -- the C-2 public stage key set -- is STRICTLY NARROWER than the live schema it cites. Three stage fields the live C-2 schema declares are therefore neither instantiated by the probe descriptor nor admitted by the instrument: budget, providerId and probeId. The measurement's admitting set is consequently an UNDER-count at those positions, which is the opposite of the direction RT24-A-RES-08's statement gives a reader.

measured.derivedFrom: c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json@sha256:4876284790462968549f834b866c7ffc5f7be1c43b583169570c1947c5c4af39 #stageSchemas: common.required + common.optional + the union over kinds{fact-derivation, rule-evaluation, policy-evaluation, probe}.required/.optional
measured.shardAssignmentCorrectlyExcluded: shardAssignment appears in a C-2 plan fixture but is in stageSchemas.privateOperators.names, so its exclusion from the literal is correct, not an omission.

demonstratedAgainstTheSubjectsOwnInstrum: probe['workflow']['stages'][0]['providerId'] = 'DURABLE_RETAINED' -> v24 plan.admit REFUSES with PLAN_ID_PREIMAGE_SCHEMA_VIOLATION; the reviewer's independent implementation ADMITS and mints a PlanId differing from the probe base.
Same with the RETENTION-POLICY-ID-V1 text as the value: v24 REFUSES, reviewer ADMITS.
consequencesPrecisely: $.workflow.stages[*].providerId is a free-string slot in the live C-2 schema (fixture values include 'rust-semantic', 'typescript-semantic', 'gitleaks', 'scanner.external'). It is an ADMITTING value-substitution position. It is absent from closureMeasurement.admittingShapes and therefore from hostNonWiringRule.measuredAdmittingShapes.
$.workflow.stages[*].probeId is the same. Absent from both lists.

$.workflow.stages[*].budget is closed by C-2 to StageBudgetV1 {unit, limit} (wireTypes.stageBudgetV1, closed: true), so it is NOT a further open sub-structure -- but budget.limit accepts any integer 1..2^63-1, so it admits the measurement's own integer rendering '1'. Absent from both lists.

The probe descriptor instantiates only fact-derivation, rule-evaluation and policy-evaluation stages. It never instantiates a `probe`-kind stage or a StageBudgetV1. The method's step 3 -- 'instantiates ONE occurrence of every structure the contract declares' -- is therefore not satisfied for workflow, and the shortfall is invisible because the literal refuses the missing fields as unknown keys.
nonBlockingObservations.whyTheAnchoringArgumentDoesNotCoverIt: RT24-A-RES-08 says the literal is 'anchored by the contract's own negative golden reject-workflow-unknown-field'. That golden injects `privateOperator`, which is in C-2's privateOperators.names. ANY key set that excludes private operators satisfies it. The golden anchors that the literal is not absurdly permissive; it cannot anchor completeness, and a 9-key literal and a 12-key one pass it identically. The reviewer confirmed the golden passes against the live literal.
nonBlockingObservations.whyRT24_A_RES_08sDirectionClaimIsWrong: Its statement reads: the instrument 'deliberately implements no rule whose other side is outside the pinned closure, which overstates the admitting set in the safe direction.' STAGE_KEYS is precisely such a rule: its other side is c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json, which $.recordedInputs.citedNotGated classifies RECORDED-ONLY -- cited, not hard-pinned. The residual names that file itself in theOneLiteral. So the residual contradicts its own statement two sentences later, and the safe-direction conclusion does not extend to the literal. The unimplemented joins in rulesDeliberatelyNotImplemented do overstate in the safe direction; the literal understates.
nonBlockingObservations.aCompensatingOverstatementExists: The literal is a bare subset test with no per-kind rules, so the instrument does NOT enforce C-2's kind enum or its per-kind required/forbidden lists. The reviewer set stages[0].kind = 'retention-DURABLE_RETAINED' and gave a rule-evaluation stage a forbidden `operator`; v24 ADMITTED both. That is an overstatement in the safe direction and is why $.workflow.stages[*].kind appears in admittingShapes. The two errors do not cancel -- they are at different positions -- but their coexistence is why the net count error is small.
whyThisIsNotBLOCKING: RT24-A-INV-08's statement is UNIVERSALLY QUANTIFIED and that quantifier comes first: 'The host never places the policy object, its posture or its identity at ANY position of the PLAN-ID-V1 preimage.' hostNonWiringRule.statement opens the same way. providerId, probeId and budget.limit are positions of the preimage and are therefore forbidden by the rule, notwithstanding their absence from the measured list. This is exactly the repair the predecessor review prescribed -- 'state it as a closed rule over PLAN-ID-V1 preimage positions rather than an enumeration of sinks' -- and it is what makes this finding structurally different from IR-RT23-01, where INV-08 enumerated four sink kinds and a capability grant was none of them. Nothing here is left unprotected.

The literal is DISCLOSED by name, by file, by application method (subset test) and by count. A reader who follows RT24-A-RES-08's own pointer to c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json reaches this discrepancy in minutes, as this reviewer did. The artifact under-analyses the literal; it does not conceal it.
The magnitude is 3 positions against 191 probed and 100 admitting shapes, and 2 of the 3 are free-string slots of a kind already abundantly represented in the admitting set.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: Either (a) read the stage key set from c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json#stageSchemas at run time and promote it from RECORDED-ONLY to hard-pinned, making all 17 key sets live; or (b) keep the literal, correct it to the live 12, extend build_probe_descriptor to instantiate a probe-kind stage and a StageBudgetV1, and rewrite RT24-A-RES-08's statement so the direction claim is scoped to rulesDeliberatelyNotImplemented and the literal's own direction is stated separately and correctly. Option (a) also removes the residual entirely and changes planIdClosedKeySetsThatAreCheckerSideLiterals to 0. Either way $.recordedInputs.citedNotGated's role string for c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json should be corrected: it currently reads 'cited for the request-validation / attempt-admission boundary' and omits that the file is also the source of record for the one closed key set the instrument could not read.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: $.resolvedConfiguration[*].value is a sixth open sub-structure by v24's own definition, and the subject's own plan_admit admits an arbitrary injected key into it. The published count planIdOpenSubStructures: 5 and the sentence 'Every open sub-structure in the preimage -- that is the honest answer, and it is not two' are therefore wrong on the artifact's own bytes.
nonBlockingObservations.theDefinitionApplied: v24: 'A sub-structure is open when the contract closes the map that CONTAINS it but enumerates no member set for the map ITSELF.' preimageFields tag 5 closes the ROW to {path, value, decidingLayer, analysisAffecting=true}. It places no type on `value` and enumerates no member set for it. fieldCanonicalization.resolvedConfiguration constrains sorting, uniqueness, decidingLayer and analysisAffecting -- never the value's shape. CVE1 encodes string-keyed maps.
measuredAgainstTheSubjectsOwnInstrument: value = {'retentionPosture': 'DURABLE_RETAINED'} -> v24 plan.admit ADMITS, minting a PlanId differing from the probe base. Reviewer's implementation agrees.
nonBlockingObservations.rootCause: _closure_positions classifies a position by the RUNTIME TYPE of the value the probe put there. build_probe_descriptor writes an int (1000) and a string ('strict') into the two resolvedConfiguration rows, so `value` is walked as an int slot and a string slot and never as a map. The family assignment -- and hence membership in openSubStructures rather than in the value-substitution list -- is decided by the probe's authored instantiation, which the artifact itself names as 'the one authored choice in the measurement'.
nonBlockingObservations.theIrony: v24's stated thesis is that enumerations go stale and measurements do not, and it replaces the predecessor's enumeration with a measurement. openSubStructures is the one list in the repair that still behaves like an enumeration, because its membership depends on an authored parameter rather than on the contract. It is the exact place the predecessor failed, one level up.
nonBlockingObservations.whyThisIsNotBLOCKING: $.resolvedConfiguration[*].value IS in closureMeasurement.admittingShapes and IS in hostNonWiringRule.measuredAdmittingShapes. The exposure is measured, the position is in the sink set, and RT24-A-INV-08's universal quantifier forbids the placement regardless. What is falsified is a descriptive sub-count and one sentence, not the protection. IR-RT23-01 was blocking because the sink set itself omitted an entire preimage field; nothing here is omitted from the sink set.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: Instantiate resolvedConfiguration with three rows -- an int value, a string value and a MAP value -- so the walk reaches the map, and let the measurement report 6. No change to any rule, to INV-08, or to the wiring rule. The count is the output of the run, so it repairs itself once the probe reaches the position.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: The three-layer repair closes the predecessor's exact attack and six variants. Three attacks still reach green: (1) appending a FALSE sentence composed entirely of that residual's own recomputed metric values; (2) stating a false claim in SPELLED-OUT numerals, which the digit regex cannot see; (3) editing any residual field other than measuredBoundary -- statement, whyNotRepairedHere, theOneLiteral -- none of which is bound at all.
demonstrated: Appending ' 0 of the 5 open sub-structures is reachable by any host wiring path, and 39 of 39 refusals are contract-enforced.' to RT24-A-RES-01.measuredBoundary: every digit is a genuine recomputed value of that residual's own metrics, all four checker-owned clauses still appear verbatim, the sentence is false, and the checker exits 0.
Appending ' In substance there are zero open sub-structures and every position is refused.': exits 0. _BOUNDARY_NUMBER matches digits only.
Inverting 'overstates' to 'understates' in RT24-A-RES-08.statement: exits 0, no numbers touched.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: This is materially narrower than the predecessor's defect, where the whole boundary could be rewritten into self-contradiction. The mechanism achieves its stated purpose -- each quantity stated in the role it was measured in -- and the residual is that a boundary can be EXTENDED with falsehood rather than REWRITTEN into it. Worth recording because the residual ledger is the main thing a reader of this artifact trusts, and because item (3) means the sentence carrying RT24-A-RES-08's direction claim -- the one this review found to be wrong -- sits in an unbound field.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: Extend the closure layer to reject any sentence in measuredBoundary that is not part of a rendered clause, or bind measuredBoundary to be the concatenation of its clauses plus declared free text. Number-word normalisation would close the spelled-out variant.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: v24 detects, measures and publishes a self-contradiction in a binding artifact (RESOLVED-INPUTS describes capabilityGrant with 4 keys at preimage tag 10 and 5 in nestedClosure) and declares which statement its instrument obeys. It does not file a successor request. The corpus's own precedent for a defect in a contract one does not own is v23's D9 handling: REQUESTED-NOT-ADDED with a complete proposal.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItDoesNotBlock: See centralClaimAdjudications C3. Freeze section 8's escalation limb is stated as a property -- 'a detected conflict with a binding artifact' -- and therefore already covers this without amendment; the section's own added text of 2026-08-03 makes exactly that point about IR-C2V4-01. The disagreement is a recomputed metric bound into RT24-A-RES-08's boundary clause, so it cannot go stale silently. The reading chosen is the permissive one and the closure conclusion is identical under either.
nonBlockingObservations.theGap: $.authority carries mayAmendD9Vocabulary: false, mayAmendOperabilityGates: false and mayAmendThreatModel: false, but no entry for RESOLVED-INPUTS -- the one contract in which a conflict was actually detected. The disclaimer exists only in prose. And no successor request states which of the two conflicting statements is believed defective, so a future RESOLVED-INPUTS author has a measurement but no proposal.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: Add mayAmendResolvedInputs: false to $.authority, and add a RESOLVED-INPUTS successor request in the REQUESTED-NOT-ADDED shape, quoting both statements verbatim and proposing which should govern. Neither touches RESOLVED-INPUTS and neither changes any measurement.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: Automation can reach durable retention by two distinct paths. RT24-A-RES-06 names the first (a composition declaring itself interactive, driven by a pty). RT24-A-RES-07 measures the second (a host-owned policy file whose presence makes ci cell 6 proceed durable, over 'an out-of-worktree, UNREVIEWED, host-owned file'). Both are recorded; no statement puts them together as two routes to the same outcome, and RT24-A-RES-06's framing -- terminals -- can read as though it bounds the whole automated-consent question.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: ConsentRecordV1 is self-attested: nothing binds consentRecordRef to a real interaction, and ProjectRetentionPolicyV1's retentionPolicyId is derived from projectId, posture and consentRecordRef, so a well-formed policy asserting DURABLE_RETAINED is constructible by anyone with write access to host-owned project storage.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItDoesNotBlock: Both paths are individually recorded with measured values, and RT24-A-RES-07's 'unreviewed' carries the acknowledgement that the file's provenance is not established. This reviewer does not assert that binding the policy to verifiable consent is achievable or in scope; the artifact is IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED and no host exists.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: One sentence in RT24-A-RES-06 pointing at RT24-A-RES-07 as the non-terminal route to the same outcome.

nonBlockingObservations.severity: non-blocking; correctly disclosed in the method
nonBlockingObservations.statement: The walk enumerates maps, arrays of strings and STRING slots only (_closure_positions lines 867-881). Integer, boolean and null slots are not positions. The value-substitution trials use only string renderings, while the key-injection trials additionally try the integer rendering 1. So an integer slot that would accept the policy's integer rendering is never probed.
nonBlockingObservations.isItDisclosed: YES, precisely, in closureMeasurement.method step 4: 'Every map, every array of strings and every string slot is a position.' The scope limit is stated in the method sentence rather than in whatThisMeasurementDoesNotSettle.
nonBlockingObservations.materiality: Low. The reviewer confirmed $.resolvedConfiguration[0].value = 1 is ADMITTED and mints a differing PlanId, but $.resolvedConfiguration[*].value is already in admittingShapes via the string row, so no admitting SHAPE is missed by this limit within the probe as built. The one place it would have mattered -- $.workflow.stages[*].budget.limit -- is unreachable for the separate reason in IR-RT24-N01.
nonBlockingObservations.narrowestRepair: Add integer and boolean slots to the walk and the integer rendering to value-substitution trials, or move the scope limit into whatThisMeasurementDoesNotSettle where a reader looking for limits will find it.

v10Item3Position.question: Does V10 requiredResolution item 3's discharge hold on these bytes?
v10Item3Position.ruling: YES -- it holds on these bytes, on a basis this review states exactly, part re-earned and part inherited.
v10Item3Position.whatTheArtifactClaims: claimedStatus DISCHARGEABLE-PENDING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, with predecessorReviewOutcome.appliesToTheseBytes: false and DISCHARGED explicitly listed under notClaimed. The artifact does NOT claim the discharge travelled.
v10Item3Position.whyTheDischargeDoesNotTravelAutomaticall: The predecessor review binds its Part B verdict and its discharge 'to the exact digests recorded above and to nothing else'. Those digests are v23's. Byte-identity of Part B is a necessary condition for the underlying work to survive, not a transfer of verdict. v24 enforces predecessorPartBVerdictAppliesToTheseBytes: false at line 1520 rather than merely declaring it.
whyItNeverthelessHoldsHere: The condition the predecessor set was explicit: 'the item becomes dischargeable when these bytes pass an independent review.' This is an independent review of these bytes and it finds Part B PASS at 0 blockers.

The substantive content of Part B is byte-identical to the content on which the predecessor review derived every load-bearing claim from scratch -- recomputing both sealed unitIds and the unit-set commitment, deriving all four of v22's previously ASSERTED availability fixtures including AF-03-VERIFY-PURGED, running a two-sided control, and testing P1-P5 including 40,000 randomised multi-position trials. Findings about content remain true of identical content. That is a fact about bytes, not a borrowed verdict.

This reviewer verified the byte-identity independently rather than accepting it: canonical sha256:199b55e1..., 42,255 canonical bytes and 48,011 pretty bytes on both sides, deep-equal, key order identical.

This reviewer verified that the NEW instrument still enforces Part B's guards, which byte-identity alone does not establish: nine distinct Part B value mutations each produced findings under --part b, and the carry guard additionally fired on every one.

The one Part B defect this reviewer found -- PB-CX-18's declared expectedFindingId not matching the asserted one -- is inside the carry, is exempted by a declared rule, is counted rather than hidden in RT24-RES-CORPUS-04, and is a fixture-bookkeeping mismatch rather than a semantic error.
v10Item3Position.whatThisReviewDidNotRedo: This reviewer did NOT rewrite an independent UNIT-ID-V3 / effective_capability implementation and did not re-derive the four availability fixtures from v22's sealed bytes. That work was done by the predecessor review over byte-identical content and is inherited here, and it is named as inherited. If that derivation were wrong, this review would not have caught it.
v10Item3Position.scopeOfTheDischarge: Item 3 discharges as an architecture-candidate obligation at evidenceGrade IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED. It does NOT discharge V10 as a whole -- items 1 and 2 are untouched and item 2 remains partially discharged. It does NOT unblock CD-RT-5, which remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. It does NOT constitute a product decision and does NOT assert that any implementation exists.
v10Item3Position.isItem3sDischargeInQuestionBecauseOfTheC: NO. The dispatch's condition was: if the carry is not byte-identical, Part B's verdict does not transfer and item 3's discharge is in question. The carry IS byte-identical, verified independently. The discharge is not in question on that ground.
v10Item3Position.cdRt5: UNCHANGED: BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. This review changed no status anywhere.
